To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HIV serological status is the most relevant factor in predicting visual function in HIV-infected subjects.

the HIV seropositivity is the best predictor for visual loss in the HIV-infected subjects, that this visual loss is more evident in stressful and real-life situations, that the Central Vision Analyzer may better correlate with daily living activities, and that the visual loss correlates with the loss of retinol nerve fiber layer thickness.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Central Vision Analyzer test is more sensitive than the ETDRS test in identifying visual impairment in PLWH.

the HIV-seropositive patients have a higher incidence of visual impairment in the presence of HIV-related retinal neurodegenerative disorders, and that this impairment is correlated with retinal nerve fiber loss, especially in the temporal inferior sector.
HIV serostatus, and not the nadir CD+4 count, is the best predictor for the development of neuroretinal disorder in PLWH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV infection is a risk factor for visual impairment, and that the Central Vision Analyzer is a useful tool to assess visual impairment in PLWH.
the Central Vision Analyzer may help to diagnose visual loss and to understand its pathophysiological mechanisms.
HIV-associated visual impairment can be assessed in a more realistic and time-dependent way, and may correlate with retinal neuro-axonal loss.
The main takeaway from our work is that

visual function is impaired in PLWH, even in the absence of retinitic lesions, and that the Central Vision Analyzer test may be useful to assess visual function in PLWH in multiple light/contrasts conditions.
the Central Vision Analyzer may offer a better way to evaluate vision in HIV-infected subjects, since this program tests vision in real-life situations, and is more sensitive than the ETDRS protocol.

visual function in PLWH should be tested with a computerized interactive program to simulate stressful and real-life conditions, rather than the standard ETDRS chart, which does not test visual performance in a time-dependent manner.
